title: Expire structured server events through the existing cleanup command

gates.name: Python typecheck
gates.command: docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend python -m mypy src/face_moment

gates.name: Structured event retention tests
gates.command: docker compose run --rm backend python -m pytest tests/diagnostics/test_server_event_retention.py tests/diagnostics/test_retention_cleanup.py tests/diagnostics/test_retention_api.py tests/diagnostics/test_server_event_search.py

verify.summary: Autopilot repeated the dependent-blocking pass and blocked TASK-093 because dependency TASK-091-T3-FT-009-W2 is blocked by failed TASK-090.

The explicit owner removed the obsolete failed-chain block after TASK-094 replaced the unfinished TASK-090 outcome. TASK-093 remains ordinary planned future work behind TASK-091 and has not been executed or promoted to ready.
verify.resume_route: /exe TASK-093-T3-FT-009-W3 only after TASK-091 is done and a future explicit scheduler or operator selection

evidence_required: FT-009-AC-003 RED: with the accepted server-event collection and staff search route present, the existing cleanup exposes a 30-day technical cutoff but leaves server_events untouched and technical_logs_deleted fixed at zero, so current and bookmarked browser searches still render old correlated and uncorrelated rows; GREEN: the existing owner-ordered command passes the fixed UTC cutoff to diagnostics, deletes only owner rows strictly before it including uncorrelated events, preserves equal/newer rows, records the confirmed newly deleted count in the unchanged latest-result shape, sanitizes failure and converges on safe rerun, while playwright cli proves current and bookmarked searches cannot recover deleted content; decisive comparison: disposable before/equal/after correlated/uncorrelated rows plus latest-result, repository and real-browser reads across success, injected owner failure, overlap and rerun; artifact: destructive retention evidence plus redacted Playwright transcript/screenshots under .tasks/TASK-093-T3-FT-009-W3/.
purpose: Complete the accepted technical-event lifecycle by extending the already deployed owner-ordered retention command rather than introducing another scheduler, result model or delete owner.
success_outcome: Structured server events strictly older than 30 days are deleted by diagnostics, the existing promo latest result reports the confirmed count, failure/rerun remains truthful and no current or stale search can reconstruct deleted content.
anti_goals: Do not add a second cleanup command/timer, request-triggered deletion, per-event tombstones, cleanup history, jobs table or internal scheduler.
Do not delete promo Attempts/evidence directly, change their 90-day claim, mutate the latest-result schema or cross ownership boundaries.
Do not run against production/operator data, alter production timer configuration or implement server-event collection/search behavior beyond the retention integration delta.

forbidden_scope: Production PostgreSQL, operator/default Attempts/evidence/events and production timer configuration
Direct diagnostics deletion by promo, foreign-row/cascade deletion and mutation of the existing latest-result schema
FT-009 collection/search implementation changes, FT-010 annotations, FT-011 Calibration and Photo retention/purge
stop_conditions: Event expiry cannot remain diagnostics-owned and independent of Attempt candidates through the existing promo cleanup orchestration/result.
Safe failure/rerun would require a second scheduler, history/jobs lifecycle, cross-owner transaction or fabricated deletion count.
The real current/bookmarked staff-search proof cannot use the completed TASK-091 route without modifying its search behavior or inheriting its feature claims.
Expired rows could be reconstructed through the current/stale staff page, FT-008, DiagnosticEvidence or retained task artifacts.
T3 destructive probes cannot be limited to disposable correlated/uncorrelated rows with controlled time, known state, safe rerun and complete cleanup.

constraints: Promo remains the cleanup/latest-result owner and supplies both fixed cutoffs; diagnostics alone deletes server_events and returns technical_logs_deleted through the existing result.
Delete rows with occurred_at strictly before the UTC 30-day cutoff independently of Attempt candidate IDs; equal/newer and all 90-day Attempt/evidence behavior remain unchanged.
Use the existing advisory lock, exit codes, failure sanitization, single latest-result row and external timer; add no route, command, migration or deployment change.

Use disposable correlated and uncorrelated rows with controlled before/equal/after times, owner failure, overlap, partial convergence, safe rerun, decisive search/result reads and cleanup limited to fixtures.

Use playwright cli against the implemented GET /staff/server-events route for one current search and the same bookmarked filter URL before/after cleanup; store a redacted transcript and screenshots under .tasks/TASK-093-T3-FT-009-W3/ without adopting TASK-091 filter/authorization claims.
Retained reports contain only synthetic identifiers and aggregate counts, never production rows, credentials, participant data or unredacted failures.
invariants: Diagnostics deletes only its event/evidence rows and promo deletes only confirmed promo-owned state; no cascade or direct foreign write crosses ownership.
Thirty-day event deletion includes uncorrelated rows and never depends on the 90-day Attempt candidate set.
Failure/overlap never fabricates or replaces counts; rerun never restores events and reports only newly confirmed deletion in the successful invocation.
Expired event content cannot be reconstructed through FT-009, FT-008, DiagnosticEvidence, browser cache or task evidence.
verification_targets: Disposable controlled-time fixtures prove strict before/equal/after deletion for correlated and uncorrelated events, exact aggregate count and unchanged 90-day Attempt/evidence behavior.
Injected diagnostics failure, active-lock overlap and safe rerun prove sanitized truthful latest results, no fabricated count, owner-only writes and convergence without event restoration.

playwright cli drives one current search and the same bookmarked filter URL before/after cleanup, proving deleted event fields never reappear from FT-009, FT-008, DiagnosticEvidence, browser state or retained artifacts; the redacted transcript and screenshots stay under .tasks/TASK-093-T3-FT-009-W3/.
Source/ownership scans prove one existing command/latest result/external timer, no migration/history/jobs/tombstone/internal scheduler and no production configuration mutation.
